Content: Over the past few `text(decades)`, researchers have observed declining numbers in `text(two)` species of penguins native to the West Antarctic peninsula. New evidence is pointing to a decline in their food supply as the primary cause for the recent drops in their numbers. These penguins feed on krill, small animals that grow and develop under ice masses. The graphs below show data related to `text(two)` factors: atmospheric carbon dioxide (`text(CO)_2`) levels and Antarctic ice mass. The diagram of a generalized Antarctic food web illustrates the role of the penguins.
